title: DOM, CSS selectors and XPath: choosing a locator that does not break

videos.script: A test has to find things on the page before it can do anything with them. A button, a price, a card. {{shop}} The instruction that finds one is called a locator. This lesson is about choosing locators that still work next week. {{tree}} It starts with the page as a tree. Every element has a parent, children and attributes, and every locator is a path through that tree. {{css}} Then the two classic languages for those paths. CSS selectors, which you may know from stylesheets. And XPath, which can walk upwards and read text. {{xpath}} Then the part that matters. You write a test that finds the banana by its id, the shortest locator there is. It fails on its very first run, because the shop draws a new id every time the page loads. {{breaks}} You find a card by its position, and watch the same locator point at the wrong fruit once one more is added. {{position}} Last, you find things the way a customer does. By role and name, by the words on the screen, and by an attribute written for tests. {{stable}} And you meet Playwright refusing a locator that matches eight buttons when you meant one. That refusal protects you, and its error message is worth reading closely. {{strict}}
